programme: TCF4 (the TCF/LEF effector of canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling) driving an epithelial-mesenchymal balance module together with TBX3 (a Wnt-induced T-box factor that represses CDH1/E-cadherin and marks EMT), FHL2 (a LIM-domain β-catenin/TCF coactivator active in stromal and cancer-associated fibroblasts), and GRHL3 (an epithelial-differentiation factor whose target AXIN2 feeds back on Wnt signaling, opposing the mesenchymal shift the other three factors promote)
role_in_a: In gut epithelium, TCF4/β-catenin signaling is the core driver of crypt cell renewal and epithelial turnover; a shift in this axis would be expected to alter barrier integrity and epithelial homeostasis, which is the kind of change proposed in IBS mucosa, though this role is inferred here rather than retrieved as literature specific to IBS.
role_in_b: In lung cancer, this same axis is directly documented: TCF4/β-catenin activation promotes NSCLC growth, TBX3 marks an EMT window and associates with metastatic NSCLC, and FHL2 (including stromal FHL2 in cancer-associated fibroblasts) drives ECM remodeling, radioresistance, PI3K/AKT/mTOR-dependent growth and metastasis in NSCLC/LUSC/adenocarcinoma, with GRHL3 appearing in lung adenocarcinoma TF-target network analyses as a counterweight epithelial-identity factor.
shared_axis: The same Wnt-TCF4/EMT/epithelial-integrity wiring appears to be redeployed in both tissues toward different ends: epithelial renewal and barrier maintenance in the gut versus malignant EMT and stromal remodeling in the lung. Its recurrence across both disease networks more plausibly reflects shared developmental/epithelial-homeostasis circuitry than a specific IBS–lung-cancer disease link.
reasoning: All four carrying factors are independently placed in lung cancer by retrieved papers, and TCF4 also carries a high Open Targets association percentile in IBS itself (0.9883/2050), so the module is nameable and mostly grounded in the record rather than invented. But nothing retrieved connects IBS to lung cancer through this axis specifically — the IBS side rests on an association score plus general knowledge of gut Wnt biology, not on any retrieved mechanistic or joint-disease evidence, and gut and lung have no obvious anatomical or clinical link — so the pairing itself is unexpected rather than established or supported.
support: PMID 42135726 — TCF4/β-catenin lactylation axis promotes NSCLC via ferroptosis inhibition; PMID 38249888 — GRHL3 appears in a TF-target regulatory network analysis of lung adenocarcinoma; PMID 41136360 — FHL2 enhances ITGB1-mediated ECM remodeling driving NSCLC radioresistance; PMID 40482916 — FHL2 promotes LUSC growth/therapy resistance via PI3K/AKT/mTOR; PMID 39244734 — fibroblast FHL2 promotes lung adenocarcinoma metastasis and angiogenesis; PMID 42346508 — TBX3 marks the epithelial-mesenchymal transition window in embryonic lung development; PMID 42133899 — TBX3 studied alongside genetic alterations and metastasis burden in metastatic NSCLC survival; PMID 41479892 — TBX3 noted in an EGFR-mutant lung cancer case report. none found for IBS specifically.
how_to_falsify: In IBS colonic biopsies versus healthy controls, measure nuclear β-catenin/TCF4 activity and canonical Wnt target expression (e.g. AXIN2, LGR5); if target expression is unchanged, the proposed IBS role of this axis fails. In parallel, in an NSCLC/LUSC model, co-knock down TBX3 and FHL2 and test whether TCF4/β-catenin-driven EMT (CDH1 repression, invasion, ECM remodeling) still proceeds; if EMT is unaffected by their loss, the claim that these four factors act as one module is undermined.
caveats: Only 1 independent cohort pair underlies the 112 patient-group comparisons, so replication across genuinely separate cohorts is untested. IBS evidence for this axis is limited to an Open Targets association percentile for TCF4 alone — no IBS-specific literature was retrieved for any of the four carrying factors, consistent with the reader's note that IBS-specific evidence is largely absent. Eight of the twelve concordant factors (HOXB6, SIM2, HOXB5, TLX1, ARID5A, DEAF1, HAND1, IRF8) have no documented role in either disease and were deliberately left out of this account rather than forced into the story; HOXB6/SIM2/HOXB5 in particular have the highest recurrence fractions (83, 74, 73 of 112) yet no retrieved evidence in either disease, so recurrence alone should not be read as mechanistic relevance. The single-view exclusions (SP8, PAX9, MYCN, etc.) and tissue-generic removals confirm this account isn't built on one subgroup or an unremoved master regulator.
